text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HET FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Dutch future central bank chief Arnoud Willink calls German finance minister Waigel's plan to revalue gold stock 'the ultimate insult to a central bank'. (p1)
- Govt advisers to say Dutch budget deficit should be cut to one percent of GDP in the next cabinet term and to zero percent in future. (p1)
- Retailer Ahold wants government compensation for the cost of switching to the euro. (p1)
- MPs want to curb Libertel and PTT Telecom expanding mobile frequencies during the next three years. (p1)
- Environmentalists opposed to Schiphol airport's plans for dealing with growth of air traffic. (p5)
DE VOLKSKRANT
- Ministers of economic affairs and justice apologise for chaos in legal system resulting from the Securitel case. (p1)
- Cabinet split over environment plans for next century.
DE TELEGRAAF
- Vice-PM Tansu Ciller of Turkey has no plans to apologise to the Netherlands after it has become clear that the fire in The Hague was not a racist attack. (p1)
- Value of Dutch pensions could drop after introduction of the euro, says former junior minister of finance. (p7)
- Bank insurer Fortis introduces new investment product for large investors. (p37)
TROUW
- Public transport group VSN books lower 1996 net profit in spite of growth of number of passengers. (p7)
- Brewer Grolsch chief Paul Snoep unexpectedly resigns at the end of this year. (p7)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Machine maker Stork /ABB still in the running for a construction order to build a power plant in Curacao. (p11)
--Amsterdam newsdesk +31-20-504-5000
